The caption and text describe the same chest CT but give a single 2.5 cm size versus two axes; the source does not explain the difference (arithmetic-only, not two conflicting values of one printed dimension), so the caption CT size is review_only. The X-ray and Table 1 sizes are separate statements and are not merged.

Enlarged lymph node stations are named differently by different statements: lymph nodes 4R and 7 in the CT caption, nodes of groups 5 and 7 as metastatic at intraoperative examination. These come from different examinations and are not merged or treated as a conflict.

The reference point of the 12 months before death is not stated. Adjuvant therapy is ordered after the segmentectomy only by the word adjuvant, and before death only by the sentence order of the same sentence; no start date, regimen or duration is given.

The caption labels panels A and B jointly as pre- and postoperative chest X-rays without stating which panel is which, and the text does not say whether the preoperative film is the radiograph that first detected the tumor.

Discussion paragraphs describe the operating team layout and technique in "our material" and literature cases; unlabelled discussion sentences are not assigned to the index patient. Table 1 rows 1 to 20 are cited literature cases, not index-patient facts.

claims.text: A 56-year-old man with previously confirmed situs inversus totalis was admitted to a thoracic surgery department in January 2014 for a 2.5 cm right lung tumor of unknown etiology detected on chest X-ray. He had no clinical symptoms. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed situs inversus and showed a 28 × 22 mm tumor in the sixth right segment with a 9 mm satellite tumor and enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes.

claims.text: He qualified for surgery via right thoracotomy. Intraoperatively, left-lung anatomy was found on the right side with an undeveloped posterior interlobar fissure and nodal metastases in groups 5 and 7, and the procedure was limited to sixth segmentectomy with mediastinal and lung hilar lymphadenectomy. The final diagnosis was adenocarcinoma G2 with a partial micropapillary G3 component, T1bN2Mx/IIIA. The postoperative course was uneventful. He received adjuvant chemo- and radiotherapy and died after 12 months due to metastatic brain spread.
